title: Who played in Wingy's band, and Doc Randall and Joe Marcello
summary: Duerr and Allen try to recall Wingy's personnel such as Lanoue, Buck Scott and the trombonist; then questions about Doc Randall and Joe Marcello.

story.theme_name: Who was in the band: naming sidemen and personnel
story.community_name: Who played in the band: reciting personnel

blocks.x: He had a colored bass player. He didn't use Pop Fortier. He was a colored bass player. And he was a dealer. What's his name? A piano player. A white piano player. A raw or something. Lanoue. Lanoue. Lanoue. Lanoue. Lanoue. Yeah. What's that company of his first name? Lanoue was on piano. Conrad. Conrad, yeah. I didn't know him too well, but I know him. Conrad and... Let's see, he didn't have a big one on the trombone, did he?
No, I don't think he had a trombone.
Yeah, he had a trombone man.
But who was Buck Scott? That's the guy I wanted to ask you. Buck Scott, oh, wait a minute. Buck Scott, oh, he played later with Wayne, you know, before, I can't remember.
I don't know. Did you know him?
He was good, he was a good tailgate man, you know.
The trombone, or maybe it was him that played with the record. I don't know. I can't remember.
It may have been, you know, I just, that's the guy I always wondered about. Because he made my honey's loving arms with Wayne, you remember that? That's a good number.
He might have made them too. I can't remember.
Did he have a clarinet player?
He had one, I'm trying to think of a good voice too. He didn't think of a good voice.
And saxophone, I guess. He was a good one. And drums. Yeah.
He had some, I think he had a white guy on the trombone. I can't remember his name, but he wasn't very warm, I think.
Did you know Alex Hill, by the way? Alex Hill, yeah. He was a piano player and a rancher, he was a friend of Mads. He used to hit it kind of hard. I don't recall that.
A musical director type of man.

Yeah, no, I don't remember that. I can't remember who really had a great guy. I had a piano player. Yeah. And I know he had a colored bass player. And I went to call him, come out on piano. And he had a white drumming, but I can't remember the beat. But he wasn't going to get any going on. Yeah.

Mads talks about just throwing this guy, this radio booker named Gerald. You know, he was going to arrange all kinds of deals for him. Something about Broadway and 54th. I forget the story now. You know. I read it last week and I forget it now. Should have read it again this morning, but too much stuff happens. Was Doc Randall up there when you were there?

Yeah, Doc Randall lived with Sharpie too when he was up there. He was living with a suit. He wasn't working with Sharpie, but he was up there. Who was he working with? I don't know what he was doing. He was up in New York.
Clayton Thor, okay. I was gonna ask you some more deals I had written down here about Wingy's band. Where was Joe Marcelo working then in New York? Did he ever work?
